verses: On that jujube tree the wind, From the south, blows soft and kind, Till each twig, in inmost place, Swells with life, and shines with grace. O how great the toil and care 'Twas our mother's lot to bear!
On that jujube tree the wind, From the south, blows soft and kind, Till its branches all are seen Bright and rich in living green. Wise our mother is and good; Goodness we have never showed.
See that cool and crystal spring, How its waters comfort bring, Welling forth the city near, All who dwell in Chun to cheer! Pained our mother is and tried, As if help we seven denied.
In their yellow plumage bright, Lovely gleam those birds to sight, And their notes fall on the ear, Rich and, oh! so sweet to hear. Seven sons we, without the art To compose our mother's heart!
